==Ancestry==
=== In legend ===
[[File:Suwa Daimyōjin - 諏訪大明神.jpg|left|thumb|Suwa Daimyōjin ({{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|it|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata}}) wearing hunting gear. Religious rites centered around hunting and agriculture were an integral part of Suwa Shrine's ritual calendar in the medieval period.]]
Although the Suwa, which was the high priestly lineage of the Upper Shrine (上社 ''Kamisha'') of Suwa, one of the component shrines of [[Suwa-taisha|Suwa Grand Shrine]], traditionally regarded themselves to be the descendants of the shrine's [[Kami|deity]], [[Takeminakata]] (also known as Suwa {{ill|Myōjin|fr|Myōjin|ja|明神|ko|묘진|zh|明神|qid=Q5369590|lt=Daimyōjin}}),<ref name="Picken">{{cite book|last1=Picken|first1=Stuart D.B.|title=Historical Dictionary of Shinto|date=28 December 2010|publisher=Scarecrow Press|isbn=978-0810871724|page=288|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xlG3F6gSm9UC&pg=PA288}}</ref> the clan's actual historical origins are shrouded in mystery.

In the ''[[Kojiki]]'' and the ''[[Kujiki|Sendai Kuji Hongi]]'', Takeminakata is portrayed as a son of the god [[Ōkuninushi]] who fled to Suwa after his defeat at the hands of the god [[Takemikazuchi]], who was sent by the gods of [[Takamagahara|heaven]] to [[Kuni-yuzuri|claim the land]] held by his father in the name of the goddess [[Amaterasu]].<ref name="Chamberlain">{{cite book|last1=Chamberlain|first1=Basil|title=A translation of the "Ko-ji-ki" or Records of Ancient Matters|date=1882|url=http://sacred-texts.com/shi/kj/kj039.htm#fn_697}}</ref><ref name="Hackin1932">{{cite book|author=J. Hackin|title=Asiatic Mythology: A Detailed Description and Explanation of the Mythologies of All the Great Nations of Asia |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=HAZrFhvqnTkC&pg=PA395|year=1932|publisher=Asian Educational Services|isbn=978-81-206-0920-4|page=395}}</ref><ref name="Herbert2010">{{cite book|author=Jean Herbert|title=Shinto: At the Fountainhead of Japan|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Sg_JBQAAQBAJ&pg=PT437|date=18 October 2010|publisher=Routledge|isbn=978-1-136-90376-2|page=437}}</ref><ref name="Ashkenazi2003">{{cite book |author=Michael Ashkenazi|title=Handbook of Japanese Mythology|url=https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk|url-access=registration|date=1 January 2003 |publisher=ABC-CLIO|isbn=978-1-57607-467-1|pages=[https://archive.org/details/handbookofjapane0000ashk/page/267 267]–268}}</ref> Other myths (mostly of medieval provenance), however, portray the Suwa deity in a different light. In one story, Suwa Daimyōjin is an interloper who wrested control of Suwa from the indigenous god [[Moriya|Moriya]],<ref name="呉清恵2011">{{cite book|author=Oh|first=Amana ChungHae|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hxulspIN_2UC&pg=PA157|title=Cosmogonical Worldview of Jomon Pottery|date=November 2011|publisher=Sankeisha|isbn=978-4-88361-924-5|page=157}}</ref> the mythical ancestor of the Moriya (守矢氏) clan, one of the priestly families of the Upper Shrine.<ref name="Moriya">Moriya, Sanae (1991). ''Moriya Jinchō-ke no ohanashi'' (守矢神長家のお話し). In Jinchōkan Moriya Historical Museum (Ed.). ''Jinchōkan Moriya Shiryōkan no shiori'' (神長官守矢資料館のしおり) (Rev. ed.). pp. 2–3.</ref><ref name="JinchoMoriyaKeifu">''Jinchō Moriya-shi Keifu'' (神長守矢氏系譜), in {{cite book|editor=Suwa Kyōikukai (諏訪教育会)|title=諏訪史料叢書 巻28 (Suwa shiryō-sōsho, vol. 28)|date=1931|location=Suwa|publisher=Suwa Kyōikukai|url=http://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/1185913/24|language=ja}}</ref> In another myth, the god is said to have chosen an eight-year-old boy to become his priest (祝, ''hōri''; {{ill|Historical kana orthography|es|Uso histórico del kana|fr|Rekishiteki kanazukai|ja|歴史的仮名遣|ko|역사적 가나 표기법|ru|Историческая орфография каны|zh|歷史假名遣|qid=Q1142552|lt=historical orthography}}: ''hafuri'') and [[Shintai|living incarnation]] by clothing the latter with his own garments. This boy is eventually said to have become the founding ancestor of the Suwa clan.<ref name="Shinenpyo">Suwa Kyōikukai (1938). ''[https://books.google.com/books?id=u2Mf7Ef60FkC&pg=PA11 諏訪史年表] (Suwa Shinenpyō).'' Nagano: Suwa Kyōikukai. p. 11.{{in lang|ja}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{cite web|title=大祝有員 (Ōhōri Arikazu)|url=http://www.city.suwa.lg.jp/scm/dat/nandemo/koumoku/0300/030504.htm|website=Official website of Suwa City |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=諏方氏 (Suwa Clan)|url=http://www.city.suwa.lg.jp/scm/dat/nandemo/koumoku/0300/030503.htm|website=Official website of Suwa City |language=ja}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Yamada|first1=Taka|title=Shinto Symbols|url=http://www.dl.ndl.go.jp/view/download/digidepo_9602313_po_CRJ-187.PDF?contentNo=1&alternativeNo=|page=8}}</ref><ref name="Ihara">{{cite journal|last1=Ihara|first1=Kesao|title=鎌倉期の諏訪神社関係史料にみる神道と仏道 : 中世御記文の時代的特質について (Shinto and Buddhism as Depicted in Historical Materials Related to Suwa Shrines of the Kamakura Period : Temporal Characteristics of Medieval Imperial Writings)|journal=Bulletin of the National Museum of Japanese History|date=2008-03-31|volume=139|pages=157–185|url=https://rekihaku.repo.nii.ac.jp/?action=pages_view_main&active_action=repository_view_main_item_detail&item_id=1538&item_no=1&page_id=13&block_id=41|language=ja}}</ref>

The god declared, "I do not have a body and so make this priest (''hōri'') my body."

This [boy] is Arikazu (有員), the priest of the sacred robe (御衣祝 ''Misogihōri''), the founding ancestor of the Miwa (Jin) clan.</blockquote>However, a brief text attached to a genealogical record of the Suwa clan discovered in the ''Ōhōri''<nowiki/>'s residence in 1884<ref>Ihara (2008). p. 261.</ref> instead portrays Arikazu as a descendant of Kumako (神子 or 熊子), a son of a ''[[kuni no miyatsuko]]'' (provincial governor) of {{ill|Shinano Province|ckb|پارێزگای شینانۆ|cs|Provincie Šinano|de|Provinz Shinano|eo|Provinco Ŝinano|es|Provincia de Shinano|fa|ولایت شینانو|fr|Province de Shinano|gl|Provincia de Shinano|hak|Shinano-koet|id|Provinsi Shinano|it|Shinano (provincia)|ja|信濃国|knc|Shinano Province|ko|시나노국|lt|Šinano žemė|ms|Wilayah Shinano|nl|Shinano (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Shinano|pt|Província de Shinano|ru|Синано (провинция)|simple|Shinano Province|sk|Šinano (provincia)|sr|Провинција Шинано|th|แคว้นชินาโนะ|tr|Shinano (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сінано|zh|信濃國|zh_min_nan|Sinano-kok|zh_yue|信濃國|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}, who is claimed to have founded the Upper Shrine during the reign of {{ill|Emperor Yōmei|ar|الإمبراطور يومي|arz|الامبراطور يومى|azb|یومی (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট ইওমি|ckb|ئیمپراتۆر یۆمێی|cs|Jómei|de|Yōmei|es|Yōmei Tennō|fa|امپراتور یومی|fi|Yōmei|fr|Yōmei|id|Kaisar Yōmei|it|Yōmei|ja|用明天皇|ka|იომეი|ko|요메이 천황|nl|Yomei|pl|Yōmei|pt|Yomei|ru|Император Ёмэй|sh|Car Yōmei|simple|Emperor Yōmei|sl|Cesar Jomei|sv|Yomei|th|จักรพรรดิโยเม|tl|Emperador Yōmei|tr|Yōmei (imparator)|uk|Імператор Йомей|uz|Imperator Yōmei|vi|Thiên hoàng Yōmei|yo|Emperor Yōmei|zh|用明天皇|zh_min_nan|Yômei Thian-hông|zh_yue|用明天皇|qid=Q349281|lt=Emperor Yōmei}} (585-587).<ref name="Miwakeizu">''Ōhōri-bon Jinshi Keizu'' (大祝本 神氏系図), cited in {{cite book|last1=Kanai|first1=Tenbi|title=Suwa-shinkō-shi (諏訪信仰史)|date=1982|publisher=Meicho Shuppan|pages=107, 190}}</ref><blockquote>When Kumako was eight years old, the revered deity appeared, took off his robe and put them on Kumako. After declaring, "I do not have a body and so make you my body," he disappeared. This [Kumako] is the ancestor of Arikazu of the Miwa (Jin) clan, the ''Misogihōri''. In the second year of Emperor Yōmei, Kumako built a sanctuary at the foot of the mountain at the southern side of the lake.</blockquote>Another genealogical record, that of the [[Aso clan]] ([[:ja:阿蘇氏|阿蘇氏]]) of [[Aso Shrine]] in [[Kyushu]] (discovered in 1956), similarly identifies Otoei (乙頴) - there given the alias 'Kumako' - as the "''Ōhōri'' of the great deity of Suwa" (諏訪大神大祝) and narrates the same legend as those found above.<ref>''Ihon Asoshi Keizu'' (異本阿蘇氏系図), cited in Kanai (1982). p. 109.</ref> Recent reappraisals of these two genealogies, however, have cast doubt on their authenticity and reliability as historical sources.<ref>Ihara (2008). pp. 260-262.</ref><ref>{{cite web|author=Fukushima, Masaki (福島正樹)|title=信濃古代の通史叙述をめぐって (Shinano kodai no tsūshi jojutsu o megutte)|url=http://user1.matsumoto.ne.jp/~fukusima/yamakawa.htm|access-date=2017-09-24|website=科野太郎の古代・中世史の部屋}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Itō, Rintarō (伊藤麟太朗)|title=所謂『阿蘇氏系図』について (Iwayuru 'Aso-shi Keizu' ni tsuite)|journal=Shinano (信濃)|date=1994|volume=46|issue=8|pages=696–697|publisher=Shinano Shigakukai (信濃史学会)}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Murasaki, Machiko (村崎真智子)|title=異本阿蘇氏系図試論 (Ihon Aso-shi keizu shiron)|journal=Hito, mono, kotoba no jinruigaku: Kokubu Naoichi Hakushi beiju kinen ronbunshū (ヒト・モノ・コトバの人類学. 国分直一博士米寿記念論文集)|date=1996|pages=202–218|publisher=Keiyūsha (慶友社)}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author1=Asoshina, Yasuo (阿蘇品 保夫)|title=阿蘇社と大宮司―中世の阿蘇 (Aso-sha to Daiguji: chusei no Aso)|date=1999|publisher=Ichinomiya-machi (一の宮町)|isbn=978-4877550462}}</ref><ref>For a contrary viewpoint, cf. {{cite web|author1=Hōga, Yoshio (宝賀寿男)|title=村崎真智子氏論考「異本阿蘇氏系図試論」等を読む|url=http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/|date=2006}}</ref>

Apart from these candidates, the clan has also been claimed to descend from the {{ill|Seiwa Genji|ar|سيوا جينجي|de|Seiwa Genji|es|Seiwa Genji|fa|خاندان سیوا گنجی|fr|Seiwa-Genji|he|סיווה גנג'י|ja|清和源氏|ko|세이와 겐지|nl|Seiwa Genji|pt|Seiwa Genji|th|เซวะ เก็นจิ|tr|Seiwa Genji|vi|Seiwa Genji|zh|清和源氏|qid=Q2164991|lt=Seiwa Genji}} via Minamoto no Mitsuyasu (one of the sons of {{ill|Minamoto no Tsunemoto|fa|میناموتو نو تسونه‌موتو|fr|Minamoto no Tsunemoto|ja|源経基|ko|미나모토노 쓰네모토|oc|Minamoto no Tsunemoto|pt|Minamoto no Tsunemoto|th|มินะโมะโตะ โนะ สึเนะโมะโตะ|vi|Minamoto no Tsunemoto|zh|源经基|qid=Q3099236|lt=Minamoto no Tsunemoto}}).<ref name="Harimaya">{{cite web|title=諏訪氏 (Suwa-shi)|url=http://www2.harimaya.com/sengoku/html/suwa_k.html|website=播磨屋 (harimaya.com)|language=ja}}</ref><ref name="Papinot">{{cite book|last1=Papinot|first1=Edmond|title=Historical and Geographical Dictionary of Japan, Volume 2|date=1910|page=[https://archive.org/details/PapinotDictionaryOfJapanVolume2Complete/page/n148 611]|url=https://archive.org/details/PapinotDictionaryOfJapanVolume2Complete}}</ref>

==The Suwa ''Ōhōri''==
[[File:Suwa taisha Kamisha Maemiya , 諏訪大社 上社 前宮 - panoramio (13).jpg|thumb|''Kamisha Maemiya'', one of the two main shrines that comprise the Upper Shrine of Suwa. The Upper Shrine's high priest or ''Ōhōri'' resided in this area during the medieval period.]]
In antiquity, the Suwa clan produced the Upper Shrine (上社 ''Kamisha'') of Suwa's high priest known as the ''Ōhōri'' (大祝 'great priest', {{ill|Historical kana orthography|es|Uso histórico del kana|fr|Rekishiteki kanazukai|ja|歴史的仮名遣|ko|역사적 가나 표기법|ru|Историческая орфография каны|zh|歷史假名遣|qid=Q1142552|lt=old orthography}}: おほはふり ''Ohohafuri''; also rendered as ''Ōhafuri''), who was worshiped as [[Arahitogami|the living avatar]] of the shrine's deity during his period in office.<ref name="Ihara"/><ref>{{cite book|title=The Cambridge History of Japan, Volume 1: Ancient Japan|year=1988|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=978-0521223522|page=343|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=A3_6lp8IOK8C&pg=PA343}}</ref>

The ''Ōhōri'', who traditionally assumed the position at a young age (ideally between the ages of eight to fifteen), was assisted [[Suwa taisha#Priests|by five priests]] headed by the ''Jinchōkan'' (神長官) of the Moriya clan, who oversaw the Upper Shrine's religious rituals, many of which are centered around the worship of [[:en:List of agricultural gods|agricultural]] and {{ill|List of fertility deities|es|Anexo:Deidades de la fertilidad|eu|Zerrenda:Emankortasunaren jainkosak|fa|فهرست خدایان باروری|fr|Liste des déesses de la fertilité|id|Daftar deifikasi kesuburan|pa|ਜਣਨ ਦੇਵਤਿਆਂ ਦੀ ਸੂਚੀ|ru|Список божеств плодородия|sco|Leet o growthiness deities|tr|Doğurganlık tanrıları listesi|qid=Q2668203|lt=fertility god(s)}} called [[Mishaguji]]. The ''Jinchōkan'' was believed to have the prerogative to {{ill|Spirit possession|am|የዛር መንፈስ|ar|استحواذ روحي|cdo|Huăng-gūi|de|Besessenheit|el|Δαιμονοληψία|es|Posesión espiritual|fa|تسخیر روح|fi|Riivaus|fr|Possession (anthropologie)|fy|Geastlike besetting|he|איחוז|hr|Opsjednuće|hu|Megszállottság (vallás)|id|Kerasukan|it|Possessione|ja|憑依|ko|빙의|ms|Kerasukan|nl|Bezetenheid|pl|Opętanie|pt|Possessão espiritual|ru|Одержимость|sh|Posednutost|simple|Spirit possession|sr|Поседнутост духом|tl|Pagsapi ng demonyo|tr|Posesyon|uk|Одержимість|vi|Nhập hồn|war|Pagtag-iya hin espiritu .|zh|附身|zh_yue|鬼上身|qid=Q1782082|lt=summon the Mishaguji onto individuals and objects}} whenever its presence was called for.<ref name="Moriya 2">Moriya, Sanae (1991). ''Moriya-jinchō-ke no ohanashi'' (守矢神長家のお話し). In Jinchōkan Moriya Historical Museum (Ed.). ''Jinchōkan Moriya Shiryōkan no shiori'' (神長官守矢資料館のしおり) (Rev. ed.). p. 4. {{in lang|ja}}</ref><ref>Miyasaka, Mitsuaki (1987). "Kyodai naru kami no kuni. Suwa-shinkō no tokushitsu (強大なる神の国―諏訪信仰の特質)." In Miyasaka, Mitsuaki (1987). "Kyodai naru kami no kuni. Suwa-shinkō no tokushitsu (強大なる神の国―諏訪信仰の特質)." In {{cite book|author1=Ueda|author2=Gorai|author3=Ōbayashi|author4=Miyasaka, M.|author5=Miyasaka, Y.|title=御柱祭と諏訪大社 (Onbashira-sai to Suwa-taisha)|location=Nagano|publisher=Chikuma Shobō|isbn=978-4480841810|pages=25–26|language=ja}}</ref>

Though officially the Upper Shrine's chief priest and as incarnate deity, an object of worship, the Suwa ''Ōhōri'' had little, if any, actual power over the shrine's affairs, which rested in the hands of the Moriya ''Jinchōkan'', with his unique relationship to the Mishaguji and his knowledge of closely guarded secret traditions passed down via word of mouth only to the heir to the office.<ref>Moriya (1991), p. 5.</ref> In fact, it was due to the ''Jinchōkan'' summoning the Mishaguji onto the ''Ōhōri'' during the investiture ceremony that the latter became a living deity.<ref>{{cite web|title=ミシャグジ (Mishaguji)|url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E3%83%9F%E3%82%B7%E3%83%A3%E3%82%B0%E3%82%B8.html|website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)|language=ja}}</ref><ref>Miyasaka (1987). p. 29.</ref>

===Investiture ceremony===
The full rite of investiture into the office of ''Ōhōri'' as practiced in the late medieval period involved the candidate first undergoing a twenty-two day period of strict [[ritual purification]] in the ''Maemiya'' (前宮 'old shrine'), one of the Upper Shrine<nowiki />'s two component shrines. During the day of the ceremony itself, the ''Jinchōkan'' led the candidate by the hand before a sacred tree west of the ''Gōdono'' (神殿), the ''Ōhōri''<nowiki />'s residence during his term located west of the ''Maemiya'', under which was a flat rock known as the ''kanameishi'' (要石 'keystone'). During the ceremony, this rock is surrounded a makeshift enclosure or hut and a mat of reeds was placed over it for the boy to sit on.<ref>Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 722.</ref>

Inside this enclosure, the ''Jinchōkan'' dressed the boy in full ritual attire: traditional makeup (''{{ill|Oshiroi|ar|أوشيروي|de|Oshiroi|es|Oshiroi|fr|Oshiroi|ja|おしろい|ko|오시로이|ru|Осирои|zh|白粉 (化妝品)|qid=Q1720834|lt=oshiroi}}'', ''{{ill|Ohaguro|ar|أوهاجورو|de|Ohaguro|es|Ohaguro|fi|Ohaguro|fr|Ohaguro|hu|Ohaguro|hy|Օհագուրո|id|Ohaguro|it|Ohaguro|ja|お歯黒|ko|오하구로|ru|Охагуро|sv|Ohaguro|uk|Охагуро|qid=Q2016382|lt=Ohaguro}}'', ''{{ill|Rouge (cosmetics)|ar|روج (مستحضر تجميلي)|bew|Kelir pipi|bg|Руж|da|Rouge|de|Rouge (Kosmetik)|el|Ρουζ|eo|Ruĝiga ŝminko|es|Colorete|et|Ruuž|fa|رژ گونه|fi|Poskipuna|fr|Fard (maquillage)|fy|Rûzje (make-up)|he|סומק (איפור)|hy|Կարմրաներկ|id|Perona pipi|io|Fardo|it|Fard|ja|頬紅|ko|블러셔|ku|Algûne|ms|Pemerah pipi|mzn|آلغونه|nl|Rouge (make-up)|no|Rouge|pl|Róż (kosmetyk)|pt|Blush|ru|Румяна|simple|Blush|sr|Руменило за лице|sv|Rouge (smink)|tr|Allık|uk|Рум'яна|vi|Phấn má hồng|zh|胭脂|zh_yue|胭脂|qid=Q181791|lt=beni}}'' and ''{{ill|Hikimayu|es|Hikimayu|hy|Հիկիմայու|ja|引眉|ka|ჰიკიმაიუ|pt|Hikimayu|ru|Хикимаю|simple|Hikimayu|zh|黛眉|qid=Q11009850|lt=mayuzumi}}''), a dull yellow-green ''[[sokutai]]'', a ''{{ill|Hakama|ar|هاكاما|ca|Hakama|da|Hakama|de|Hakama|el|Χακάμα|eo|Hakamo|es|Hakama|fa|هاکاما|fi|Hakama|fr|Hakama|hu|Hakama|id|Hakama|it|Hakama|ja|袴|jv|Hakama|ka|ჰაკამა|ko|하카마|mk|Хакама|ms|Hakama|nl|Hakama|pa|ਹਾਕਾਮਾ|pl|Hakama|pt|Hakama|ru|Хакама|simple|Hakama|sq|Hakama|sr|Хакама|sv|Hakama|tr|Hakama|uk|Хакама|vi|Hakama|zh|袴 (和服)|qid=Q164668|lt=Hakama}}'', and a crown (''kanmuri'').<ref>Fujimori, Akira (1991). ''Ōhōri sokui no keshō-dōgu'' (大祝即位の化粧道具). In Jinchōkan Moriya Historical Museum (Ed.). ''Jinchōkan Moriya Shiryōkan no shiori'' (神長官守矢資料館のしおり) (Rev. ed.). p. 37. {{in lang|ja}}</ref> The ''Jinchōkan'' then summoned the Mishaguji (who as a [[:en:nature spirit|nature spirit]] was believed to manifest on rocks and trees<ref name="Moriya 2" />) to the ''kanameishi'' via secret {{ill|Mantra|af|Mantra|als|Mantra|ar|مانترا|az|Mantra|ban|Mantra|bar|Mantra|be|Мантра|bg|Мантра|bn|মন্ত্র|bo|མན་རྡ་ར།|bxr|Тарни|ca|Mantra|cs|Mantra|cy|Mantra|da|Mantra|de|Mantra|dty|मन्त्र|el|Μάντρα|eo|Mantro|es|Mantra|et|Mantra|eu|Mantra|fa|مانترا|fi|Mantra|fr|Mantra|gl|Mantra|gn|Mantra|gu|મંત્ર|he|מנטרה|hi|मन्त्र|hu|Mantra|hy|Մանտրա|ia|Mantra|id|Mantra|it|Mantra|ja|マントラ|ka|მანტრა|kk|Мантра|kn|ಮಂತ್ರ|ko|만트라|ks|مَنتَر|la|Mantra|lmo|Mantra|lt|Mantra|lv|Mantra|mag|मन्त्र|min|Mantra|ml|മന്ത്രം|mn|Тарни|mr|मंत्र|ms|Mantera|ne|मन्त्र|new|मन्त्र|nl|Mantra|nn|Mantra|no|Mantra|pa|ਮੰਤਰ|pi|मन्त्र|pl|Mantra|pnb|منتر|pt|Mantra|ro|Mantra|ru|Мантра|sa|मन्त्रः|sco|Mantra|sh|Mantra|si|මන්තර|simple|Mantra|sk|Mantra|sl|Mantra|sq|Mantra|sr|Мантра|su|Mantra|sv|Mantra|ta|மந்திரம் (இந்து சமயம்)|te|మంత్రము|th|มนตร์|tok|kalama Manta|tr|Mantra|tt|Мантра|uk|Мантра|ur|منتر|vi|Chân ngôn|wuu|曼特罗|xal|Тәрнс|xmf|მანტრა|zh|曼怛羅|qid=Q131510|lt=incantations}}. Via the rock, the Mishaguji was then believed to enter the child's body, thereby turning him into a [[Arahitogami|living god]].<ref>Miyasaka (1992). p. 53.</ref><ref name="Miyasaka2829">Miyasaka (1987). p. 28-29.</ref>

[[File:Suwa taisha Kamisha Maemiya , 諏訪大社 上社 前宮 内御玉殿 - panoramio (2).jpg|thumb|left|The Uchi-no-mitama-den (内御玉殿)]]
After being consecrated, the ''Ōhōri'' visited the various shrines of the Upper Shrine complex. In another shrine in the ''Maemiya'' area, the Uchi-no-mitama-den (内御霊殿), wherein was kept the sacred treasures of the Upper Shrine (a bell, a {{ill|Bronze mirror|ca|Espill de bronze|es|Espejo de bronce|fr|Miroir en bronze|ja|銅鏡|ko|동경 (거울)|my|ကြေးမုံ|no|Bronsespeil|simple|Bronze mirror|uk|Бронзове дзеркало|zh|铜镜|qid=Q1041984|lt=mirror}}, a {{ill|Bit (horse)|an|Bocín|ar|شكيمة|br|Gweskenn|ca|Mos (equitació)|cs|Udidlo|cv|Çăварлăх|de|Trense|eo|Mordaĵo|es|Bocado|eu|Ahoko (zaldia)|fa|عنان|fi|Kuolaimet|fr|Mors (équitation)|gd|Cabstair|he|מתג (אבזר לסוס)|hu|Zabla|id|Kekang kuda|io|Morso|it|Morso (equitazione)|ja|ハミ (馬具)|ka|ლაგამი|kn|ಕಚ್ಚುಕಂಬಿ|lt|Žąslai|nl|Bit (paard)|pl|Wędzidło|ro|Zăbală|ru|Удила|simple|Bit (horse)|sv|Bett|tr|Gem|uk|Вудила|zh|马衔|qid=Q830004|lt=bit}} and a {{ill|Saddle|an|Siella (aparello)|ar|سرج|arc|ܣܪܓܐ|ast|Siella de montar|az|Yəhər|ba|Эйәр|bg|Седло|br|Dibr|ca|Sella de muntar|chy|Hova'ó'xestôtse|cs|Jezdecké sedlo|cv|Йĕнер|cy|Cyfrwy|da|Sadel|de|Reitsattel|diq|Zên|eo|Selo|es|Silla de montar|et|Sadul|eu|Zela|fa|زین|fi|Satula|fr|Selle (équitation)|fy|Seal (hynsteriden)|gl|Sela|ha|Sirdi|he|אוכף|hi|ज़ीन|hr|Sedlo|ht|Sèl (sou cheval)|hu|Nyereg|hy|Թամբ|id|Pelana|io|Selo|is|Hnakkur|ja|鞍|ka|უნაგირი|kk|Ер|kn|ಜೀನು|ko|안장|ky|Ээр|la|Ephippium|lt|Balnas|lv|Segli|min|Palano|mn|Эмээл|ms|Pelana|myv|Камбраз|nl|Zadel (dier)|nn|Sal til dyr|no|Sal (dyr)|pl|Siodło|pms|Sela|pt|Sela|ro|Șa|ru|Седло|sah|Ыҥыыр|scn|Sedda (equitazzioni)|sco|Saidle|sh|Sedlo|simple|Saddle|sk|Jazdecké sedlo|sq|Shala e kalërimit|sr|Седло|sv|Ridsadel|ta|சேணம்|tr|Eyer|uk|Сідло|ur|زین|uz|Egar|vi|Yên|war|Lingkuranan ha hayop|wuu|鞍|zh|鞍|zh_yue|馬鞍|qid=Q192249|lt=Saddle}}) that were supposedly brought to the region by Suwa Daimyōjin himself,<ref>{{cite book|editor=Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai|title=諏訪市史 上巻 原始・古代・中世 (Suwa Shishi, vol. 1)|date=1995|location=Suwa|page=718|url=http://dl.ndl.go.jp/info:ndljp/pid/9572217}}</ref> the ''Ōhōri'' made a ritual declaration (申立 ''mōshitate'') that he has become the god's new 'body' and will henceforth avoid [[Kegare|impurity]].<ref>Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696, 722-723.</ref>

As time went on the ritual became increasingly simplified and later, was supposedly even omitted altogether, with the ''ōhōri'' simply assuming the position without any ceremony.<ref>{{cite web|title=大祝即位式場|url=http://yatsu-genjin.jp/suwataisya/zatugaku/sokui.htm|website=八ヶ岳原人}}</ref>

===Role===
During his term, the incumbent ''Ōhōri'' was treated as the physical manifestation of Suwa Daimyōjin. In 1186, [[Minamoto no Yoritomo]] officially recognized the ''Ōhōri'' as the god's incarnation in a letter to his subordinates, declaring that the ''Ōhōri''<nowiki />'s orders are those of the god himself.<ref>Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 696.</ref>

The ''Ōhōri'' was expected to live a life of ritual purity and was also forbidden to step outside the boundaries of Suwa region under pain of divine punishment.<ref>{{cite web|title=諏訪大明神 (Suwa-daimyōjin)|url=http://japangod.dip.jp/%E8%AB%8F%E8%A8%AA%E5%A4%A7%E6%98%8E%E7%A5%9E.html|website=日本の神様辞典 (Nihon no Kamisama Jiten)|language=ja}}</ref><ref name="Suwa695">Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). p. 695.</ref>

During his term of office, the ''Ōhōri'' originally resided in a building near the Suwa ''Maemiya'' known as the ''Gōdono'' (神殿). Reflecting its being the residence of an incarnate deity, the ''Maemiya'' area and its vicinity was known during the Middle Ages as the ''Gōbara'' (神原), the 'god's field'.<ref name="Tanigawa">{{cite book|editor1-last=Tanigawa|editor1-first=Kenichi|title=Nihon no kamigami: Jinja to seichi, vol. 9: Mino, Hida, Shinano (日本の神々―神社と聖地〈9〉美濃・飛騨・信濃)|date=1987|publisher=Hakusuisha|isbn=978-4560025093|pages=138–139}}</ref><ref name="Suwa695" />

Should an incumbent ''Ōhōri'' die while in office, his corpse was immediately brought before the Uchi-no-mitama-den where he was ceremonially retired - the idea being that the ''Ōhōri''<nowiki />'s spirit was temporarily deposited in the shrine until a new candidate was chosen.<ref>Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. (1995). pp. 718-719.</ref> Originally, the deceased priest was buried wearing hunting attire (such as that supposedly worn by Suwa Daimyōjin) and with hair and beard kept unshaven.<ref name="Suwa719">Suwa Shishi Hensan Iinkai, ed. pp. 719.</ref> However, in 1465, with the death of then ''Ōhōri'' Yorinaga (頼長), the local priesthood began to adopt the Buddhist custom of {{ill|Cremation|af|Verassing|ar|حرق الموتى|ast|Cremación|az|Kremasiya|be|Крэмацыя|bg|Кремация|bn|শবদাহ (ধর্মীয় আচার)|ca|Cremació|cs|Kremace|cy|Amlosgiad|da|Ligbrænding|de|Feuerbestattung|el|Αποτέφρωση των νεκρών|eo|Kremacio|es|Cremación|et|Põletusmatus|eu|Errausketa (hileta-ohikunea)|fa|آتش‌سپاری|fi|Tuhkaus|fr|Crémation|fy|Kremaasje|ga|Créamadh|gl|Cremación|he|שרפת גווייה|hi|अग्निदाह|hr|Kremacija|hu|Hamvasztás|hy|Դիակիզում|ia|Cremation|id|Kremasi|it|Cremazione|ja|火葬|jv|Krémasi|ka|კრემაცია|kk|Кремация|ko|화장 (장례)|ky|Кремация|lt|Kremacija|lv|Kremācija|mk|Кремација|ms|Pembakaran mayat|nl|Crematie|nn|Likbrenning|no|Likbrenning|pl|Kremacja|pt|Cremação|ro|Incinerație|ru|Кремация|sh|Inflamacija (antropologija)|simple|Cremation|sr|Кремација|sv|Kremering|ta|தகனம் (உடல்)|th|การเผาศพ|tr|Kremasyon|uk|Кремація|ur|احتراق نعش|vi|Hỏa táng|wuu|火葬|zh|火葬|zh_min_nan|Hóe-chòng|zh_yue|火葬|qid=Q207315|lt=Cremation}}.<ref name="Suwa719" />

By the early 17th century, the ''Ōhōri''<nowiki />'s residence was moved from the ''Maemiya'' to [https://www.google.co.jp/maps/place/%E3%80%92392-0015+Nagano-ken,+Suwa-shi,+Nakasu,+%E5%A4%A7%E7%A5%9D%E5%B1%8B%E6%95%B7/@36.000373,138.1261382,18z/data=!4m5!3m4!1s0x601c56f08ec073dd:0x2f127865a478c42a!8m2!3d36.0003473!4d138.1271388 a place] in what is now Nakasu, {{ill|Suwa, Nagano|ar|سوا (ناغانو)|azb|سووا، ناقانو|ce|Сува (гӀала)|ceb|Suwa (lungsod)|de|Suwa (Nagano)|es|Suwa (Nagano)|fa|سووا، ناگانو|fi|Suwa|fr|Suwa (Nagano)|gl|Suwa|hy|Սուվա (քաղաք)|id|Suwa, Nagano|it|Suwa|ja|諏訪市|ko|스와시|mzn|سووا، ناگانو|nl|Suwa|pl|Suwa (miasto)|pt|Suwa (Nagano)|ro|Suwa|ru|Сува (город)|sv|Suwa, Nagano|tg|Сува|th|ซูวะ|tl|Suwa, Nagano|tr|Suwa|tt|Сува (шәһәр)|uk|Сува (Наґано)|ur|سووا، ناگانو|uz|Suva (Nagano)|vi|Suwa, Nagano|war|Suwa, Nagano|zh|諏訪市|zh_classical|諏訪市|zh_min_nan|Suwa-chhī|zh_yue|諏訪|qid=Q846338|lt=Suwa City}}.

==History==
===From the Heian period to the Sengoku period===
In the meantime, other male members of the clan aside from the ''ōhōri'' - who cannot step outside the boundaries of the region, as well as come into contact with sources of impurity such as the flesh and blood of men or horses - began to pursue military careers.

One of the first recorded warriors from the clan was Tamenaka (為仲), a son of then ''ōhōri'' Tamenobu (為信). Tamenaka served under {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshiie|cs|Jošiie Minamoto|de|Minamoto no Yoshiie|es|Minamoto no Yoshiie|eu|Minamoto no Yoshiie|fa|میناموتو نو یوشی‌ایه|fr|Minamoto no Yoshiie|it|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ja|源義家|ko|미나모토노 요시이에|pt|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ro|Minamoto no Yoshiie|ru|Минамото-но Ёсииэ|sh|Minamoto no Yoshiie|sv|Minamoto no Yoshiie|th|มินาโมโตะ โนะ โยชิอิเอะ|tr|Minamoto no Yoshiie|uk|Мінамото но Йосіїе|zh|源義家|qid=Q32613|lt=Minamoto no Yoshiie}} during the [[:en:Zenkunen War|Zenkunen War]] (1051-1063) under the orders of his father, who could not participate himself due to his priestly status. He then also served again under Yoshiie in the later {{ill|Gosannen War|cs|Pozdní tříletá válka|es|Guerra Gosannen|fa|جنگ گوساننن|fr|Guerre de Gosannen|ja|後三年の役|ka|გოსანნენის ომი|ko|후3년의 역|pt|Guerra Gosannen|ru|Война Госаннэн|th|สงครามโกะซันเน็ง|uk|Трирічна війна|zh|後三年之役|qid=Q1187411|lt=Gosannen War}} of the 1080s, this time despite opposition from his family due to him already inheriting the position of ''ōhōri'' from Tamenobu in the interim between the two wars. Tamenaka's eventual suicide out of shame after his subordinates had a violent quarrel with {{ill|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|ar|ميناموتو نو يوشيميتسو|es|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|fa|میناموتو نو یوشی‌میتسو|fr|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|id|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|it|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|ja|源義光|ko|미나모토노 요시미쓰|pt|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|ru|Минамото-но Ёсимицу|tr|Minamoto no Yoshimitsu|uk|Мінамото-но Йосіміцу|zh|源義光|qid=Q3083118|lt=Minamoto no Yoshimitsu}}'s men during a feast held by the latter was considered to be divine punishment for his violation of the ban.<ref>Suwa Kyōikukai (1938). pp. 23-24.</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=源氏御家人としての諏訪氏|url=http://rarememory.justhpbs.jp/kama/na.htm#%E5%BE%8C%E4%B8%89%E5%B9%B4%E3%81%AE%E5%BD%B9%E3%81%AE%E8%AB%8F%E8%A8%AA%E7%82%BA%E4%BB%B2%E3%81%AE%E5%8E%BB%E5%B0%B1|website=信州歴史散歩}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last1=Miyachi|first1=Naokazu|title=諏訪史 第二卷 前編 (Suwa-shi, vol. 2, part 1)|date=1931|publisher=Shinano kyōikukai Suwa-bukai|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=4hBVjsO2GOgC|pages=274–275|language=ja}}</ref>

Due to the circumstances of his father's death, Tamenaka's son, Tamemori (為盛) did not inherit the office of ''ōhōri'', it instead passing in succession to Tamenaka's three younger brothers, two of whom died within mere days of their investiture. It would be the youngest brother, Tamesada (為貞), who would turn out to successfully pass down the priesthood to his progeny.

By the {{ill|Kamakura period|ar|فترة كاماكورا|be|Перыяд Камакура|bg|Камакура|bn|কামাকুরা যুগ|ckb|سەردەمی کاماکورا|cs|Období Kamakura|de|Kamakura-Zeit|eo|Kamakura-epoko|es|Período Kamakura|et|Kamakura ajastu|eu|Kamakura aroa|fa|دوره کاماکورا|fi|Kamakura-kausi|fr|Époque de Kamakura|gl|Período Kamakura|he|תקופת קמקורה|hu|Kamakura-kor|id|Zaman Kamakura|it|Periodo Kamakura|ja|鎌倉時代|ko|가마쿠라 시대|lt|Kamakura laikotarpis|mn|Камакура эрин|nl|Kamakuraperiode|no|Kamakura-perioden|pt|Período Kamakura|ru|Период Камакура|simple|Kamakura period|sk|Obdobie Kamakura|sl|Obdobje Kamakura|sr|Камакура период|sv|Kamakura|th|ยุคคามากูระ|tl|Panahong Kamakura|tr|Kamakura Dönemi|uk|Період Камакура|vi|Thời kỳ Kamakura|wuu|镰仓时代|zh|鎌倉時代|zh_min_nan|Kamakura sî-tāi|zh_yue|鎌倉時代|qid=Q236205|lt=Kamakura period}}, the clan - now renowned as being both a priestly and a warrior clan - rose to national prominence as vassals (''{{ill|Gokenin|az|Qokenin|cs|Gokenin|de|Go-kenin|es|Gokenin|fa|گوکه‌نین|fr|Gokenin|id|Gokenin|it|Gokenin|ja|御家人|ko|고케닌|ru|Гокэнин|uk|Ґокенін|vi|Gokenin|zh|御家人|qid=Q63765|lt=Gokenin}}'') of the {{ill|Kamakura shogunate|azb|کاماکورا شوگونلوغو|be|Сёгунат Камакура|ca|Shogunat Kamakura|ckb|زنجیرە شۆگنی کاماکورا|cs|Šógunát Kamakura|de|Kamakura-Shōgunat|el|Σογκουνάτο Καμακούρα|es|Shogunato Kamakura|eu|Kamakura shogunerria|fa|شوگون‌سالاری کاماکورا|fi|Kamakura-shōgunaatti|fr|Shogunat de Kamakura|hak|Kamakura mok-fú|he|שוגונות קמקורה|hu|Kamakura-bakufu|id|Keshogunan Kamakura|it|Shogunato Kamakura|ja|鎌倉幕府|ko|가마쿠라 막부|ms|Kesyogunan Kamakura|nl|Kamakura-shogunaat|no|Kamakura-shōgunatet|pl|Kamakura (okres)|pt|Xogunato Kamakura|ru|Сёгунат Камакура|simple|Kamakura shogunate|sr|Камакура шогунат|th|รัฐบาลโชกุนคามากูระ|tr|Kamakura şogunluğu|uk|Сьоґунат Камакура|vi|Mạc phủ Kamakura|zh|镰仓幕府|zh_min_nan|Kamakura bō͘-hú|zh_yue|鎌倉幕府|qid=Q736839|lt=shogunate}} and later, flourished greatly under the patronage of the {{ill|Hōjō clan|ar|عشيرة هوجو|be|Ходзё (род)|ca|Clan Hōjō|de|Hōjō|eo|Hojo (klano)|es|Clan Hōjō|eu|Hojo klana|fa|خاندان هوجو|fi|Hōjō-klaani|fr|Clan Hōjō|hu|Hódzsó család|id|Klan Hōjō|it|Clan Hōjō|ja|北条氏|ko|호조씨|ms|Puak Hōjō|nl|Hojo|no|Hōjōklanen|pl|Hōjō (ród)|pt|Clã Hōjō|ru|Ходзё (род)|sr|Клан Хоџо (Камакура)|th|ตระกูลโฮโจ|tr|Hōjō boyu|uk|Рід Ходзьо|zh|北條氏|qid=Q834364|lt=Hōjō clan}}. The clan's fortunes waned with the fall of the Kamakura shogunate and the defeat of the [[Southern Court|Southern Imperial Court]] (which the clan supported) during the {{ill|Nanboku-chō period|ar|فترة نانبوكو تشو|bg|Нанбоку-чо|bn|নান্‌বোকু-চোও যুগ|ca|Període Nanboku-chō|cs|Období Nanbokučó|de|Namboku-chō|es|Período Nanbokuchō|eu|Nanboku-chō Aroa|fa|دوره نانبوکوچو|fi|Nanboku-chō-kausi|fr|Époque Nanboku-chō|he|תקופת שתי החצרות הקיסריות|hu|A japán császári udvar különválása|id|Zaman Nanboku-chō|it|Periodo Nanboku-chō|ja|南北朝時代 (日本)|ko|남북조 시대 (일본)|ms|Tempoh Nanboku-chō|nl|Nanboku-cho-periode|pt|Período Nanboku-chō|ru|Период Намбокутё|simple|Nanboku-chō period|sr|Нанбокућо период|sv|Nanboku-chō|th|ยุคราชสำนักเหนือ-ใต้|tr|Nanboku-chō Dönemi|uk|Період Намбокутьо|vi|Nam–Bắc triều (Nhật Bản)|zh|南北朝时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Nanboku-tyô sî-tāi|zh_yue|南北朝 (日本)|qid=Q264012|lt=Nanboku-chō period}}.

During the {{ill|Muromachi period|ar|فترة موروماتشي|ast|Periodu Muromachi|bcl|Panahon nin Muromachi|be|Перыяд Мурамаці|bg|Муромачи|bn|মুরোমাচি যুগ|ceb|Panahon sa Muromachi|ckb|سەردەمی مرۆماچی|cs|Období Muromači|de|Muromachi-Zeit|eo|Epoko de Muromaĉi|es|Período Muromachi|eu|Muromachi aroa|fa|دوره موروماچی|fi|Muromachi-kausi|fr|Époque de Muromachi|gl|Período Muromachi|he|תקופת אשיקאגה|hu|Muromacsi-kor|id|Zaman Muromachi|ilo|Panahon ti Muromachi|it|Periodo Muromachi|ja|室町時代|kk|Муромачи кезеңі|ko|무로마치 시대|lt|Muromači laikotarpis|nl|Muromachiperiode|pl|Muromachi (okres)|pt|Período Muromachi|ru|Период Муромати|simple|Muromachi period|sk|Obdobie Muromači|sl|Obdobje Muromači|sr|Муромачи период|sv|Ashikaga|th|ยุคมูโรมาจิ|tl|Panahong Muromachi|tr|Muromachi Dönemi|uk|Період Муроматі|vi|Thời kỳ Muromachi|wuu|室町时代|zh|室町时代|zh_min_nan|Muromati sî-tāi|zh_yue|室町時代|qid=Q334845|lt=Muromachi period}}, the Suwa were involved both in a feud with the Kanasashi clan of the ''Shimosha'' which supported the {{ill|Northern Court|ca|Cort del Nord|cs|Severní dvůr|es|Corte del Norte|eu|Iparraldeko Gortea (Japonia)|fa|دربار شمالی|fr|Cour du Nord|id|Pemerintahan Utara|it|Corte del Nord|ja|北朝 (日本)|ko|북조 (일본)|pl|Dwór północny i południowy|pt|Corte do Norte (Japão)|ru|Северный Двор|simple|Northern Court|th|ราชสำนักเหนือ|tl|Hilagang Korte|tr|Kuzey Sarayı|uk|Північний Двір|vi|Bắc triều (Nhật Bản)|zh|北朝 (日本)|qid=Q1201819|lt=Northern Court}}, and interclan strife between the head family (惣領家 ''sōryō-ke'') and the ''ōhōri-ke'' (大祝家), a branch of the clan that had come to assume the priestly duties. With the defeat of the Kanasashi and the head family's reattainment of the position of ''ōhori'', the clan became a [[:en:Daimyō|regional power]], clashing with the [[Takeda clan]] - originally their allies - during the {{ill|Sengoku period|ar|فترة سينغوكو|arz|فتره سينجوكو|be|Перыяд Сэнгоку|bg|Сенгоку|bn|সেনগোকু যুগ|bo|སེན་གོའི་དུས་མཚམས་|ca|Període Sengoku|ckb|سەردەمی سێنگۆکو|cs|Období Sengoku|de|Sengoku-Zeit|eo|Epoko Sengoku|es|Período Sengoku|et|Sengoku ajastu|eu|Sengoku aroa|fa|دوره سنگوکو|fi|Sengoku-kausi|fr|Époque Sengoku|ga|Tréimhse Sengoku|glk|سنگؤکۊ زمات|he|תקופת סנגוקו|hu|Hadakozó fejedelemségek kora (Japán)|id|Zaman Sengoku|is|Sengoku-öldin|it|Periodo Sengoku|ja|戦国時代 (日本)|ka|სენგოკუს პერიოდი|kk|Сэнгоку дәуірі|ko|센고쿠 시대|lt|Sengoku laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Sengoku|nl|Sengokuperiode|no|Sengoku-perioden|pl|Sengoku (okres)|pt|Período Sengoku|ro|Perioada Sengoku|ru|Период Сэнгоку|sh|Sengoku razdoblje|simple|Sengoku period|sk|Obdobie Sengoku|sq|Periudha Sengoku|sr|Сенгоку период|sv|Sengoku|th|ยุคเซ็งโงกุ|tl|Panahong Sengoku|tr|Sengoku Dönemi|uk|Період Сенґоку|ur|سینگوکو دور|uz|Sengoku davri|vi|Thời kỳ Chiến Quốc (Nhật Bản)|wuu|战国时代（日本）|zh|战国时代 (日本)|zh_min_nan|Sengoku sî-tāi|zh_yue|戰國時代 (日本)|qid=Q204023|lt=Sengoku period}}. The clan again suffered a setback with {{ill|Suwa Yorishige (daimyo)|fa|سووا یوریشیگه|fr|Suwa Yorishige|it|Suwa Yorishige|ja|諏訪頼重 (戦国時代)|nl|Suwa Yorishige (Sengoku)|th|ซูวะ โยริชิเงะ|zh|諏訪賴重|qid=Q2511179|lt=Suwa Yorishige}}'s defeat in the hands of {{ill|Takeda Shingen|ar|تاكيدا شين-غن|az|Takeda Şingen|ban|Takeda Shingen|ca|Takeda Shingen|cs|Šingen Takeda|de|Takeda Shingen|eo|Takeda Shingen|es|Takeda Shingen|fa|تاکدا شینگن|fi|Takeda Shingen|fr|Takeda Shingen|hak|Takeda Shingen|he|טקדה שינגן|hu|Takeda Singen|id|Takeda Shingen|it|Takeda Shingen|ja|武田信玄|jv|Takeda Shingen|ko|다케다 신겐|nl|Takeda Shingen|no|Takeda Shingen|pl|Shingen Takeda|pt|Takeda Shingen|ru|Такэда Сингэн|sk|Šingen Takeda|sq|Takeda Shingen|sr|Такеда Шинген|sv|Takeda Shingen|th|ทาเกดะ ชิงเง็ง|tr|Takeda Shingen|uk|Такеда Шінґен|vi|Takeda Shingen|wuu|武田信玄|zh|武田信玄|zh_min_nan|Takeda Singen|zh_yue|武田信玄|zu|Takeda Shingen|qid=Q276404|lt=Takeda Shingen}} (who was, ironically, a staunch devotee of Suwa-myōjin) in 1542 and with his suicide in 1544, the extinction of the main family; his cousin Yoritada (諏訪頼忠, 1536-1606), who succeeded Yorishige's younger brother Yoritaka (諏訪頼高, 1528-1542) as ''ōhōri'', was spared. After the Takeda was destroyed by an alliance of {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|af|Oda Nobunaga|ar|أودا نوبوناغا|arz|اودا نوبوناجا|ast|Oda Nobunaga|az|Oda Nobunaqa|ban|Oda Nobunaga|bcl|Oda Nobunaga|be|Ода ===Edo period onwards===
[[File:Jinchoukan-Moriya-shiryoukan_Oohouri-bosho.JPG|thumb|230px|right|The graves of various Suwa ''ōhōri'' within the Moriya clan's estate grounds in {{ill|Chino, Nagano|ar|تشينو (ناغانو)|azb|چینو، ناقانو|ce|Тино (гӀала)|ceb|Chino (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Chino (Nagano)|eo|Ĉino|es|Chino (Nagano)|fa|چینو، ناگانو|fi|Chino (Nagano)|fr|Chino (Nagano)|gl|Chino, Xapón|hy|Տինո (քաղաք)|id|Chino, Nagano|it|Chino (Nagano)|ja|茅野市|ko|지노시|mzn|چینو، ناگانو|nl|Chino (Nagano)|pl|Chino|pt|Chino (Nagano)|ro|Chino|ru|Тино (город)|sv|Chino, Nagano|tg|Чино|th|ชิโนะ|tl|Chino, Nagano|tr|Chino, Nagano|tt|Тино (шәһәр)|uk|Тіно (Наґано)|ur|چینو، ناگانو|uz|Chino (Nagano)|vi|Chino, Nagano|war|Chino, Nagano|zh|茅野市|zh_classical|茅野市|zh_min_nan|Tino-chhī|zh_yue|茅野|qid=Q838660|lt=Chino City}}, Nagano.]]Yoritada's eldest son, Yorimizu (頼水, 1571-1641) became the first ''daimyō'' to rule {{ill|Suwa Domain|fa|قلمرو سووا|fr|Domaine de Suwa|id|Wilayah Suwa|ja|諏訪藩|pt|Domínio de Suwa|ru|Сува (княжество)|zh|諏訪藩|qid=Q3034531|lt=Suwa Domain}}, with the office of ''ōhōri'' passing down to his fourth son, Yorihiro (頼広). With this, the clan effectively split into two branches: the ''daimyō'' line and the ''ōhōri'' line. All in all, ten generations served as ''daimyō'' of Suwa Domain until the abolition of the {{ill|Han system|ca|Han (Japó)|cs|Han (Japonsko)|de|Han (Japan)|es|Han (Japón)|fa|هان (ژاپن)|fi|Daimiokunta|fr|Han (Japon)|he|האן (יחידה אדמיניסטרטיבית)|hu|Hanrendszer|id|Sistem han|it|Han (Giappone)|ja|藩|ko|번 (행정 구역)|mk|Хан (Јапонија)|ms|Sistem han|nl|Han (grondgebied)|pl|Han (Japonia)|pt|Han (território)|ru|Хан (владение)|sl|Han sistem|tr|Han (Japonya)|uk|Хан (Японія)|vi|Hệ thống các phiên|zh|藩 (日本)|qid=Q841985|lt=Han system}} during the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|ceb|Panahon sa Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096|lt=Meiji era}}.<ref>{{cite web|title=高島藩 (Takashima-han)|url=http://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~me4k-skri/han/hokuriku/takasima.html|website=Edo 300 Han HTML|language=ja}}</ref>

Meanwhile, the establishment of {{ill|State Shinto|bn|রাষ্ট্রীয় শিন্তৌ|de|Staats-Shintō|es|Sintoísmo estatal|fa|شینتوی حکومتی|fr|Shintoïsme d'État|id|Shinto Negara|ja|国家神道|ko|국가신토|no|Statsshinto|pt|Xintoísmo estatal|ru|Государственный синтоизм|simple|State Shinto|tr|Devlet Şintoizmi|vi|Thần đạo Quốc gia|zh|国家神道|qid=Q1197248|lt=State Shinto}} abolished the tradition of hereditary succession among Shinto priesthood, including that of Suwa Grand Shrine. Local clans such as the Suwa lost control of the shrine's traditional priestly offices (which in turn became defunct) as government appointees began to manage the shrine, which passed under state control.

The last Suwa ''ōhōri'', the fifteenth since Yorihiro, died in 2002 with no heirs.<ref>{{cite web|script-title=ja:最後の大祝|url=http://yatsu-genjin.jp/suwataisya/sanpo/saigo.htm|website=八ヶ岳原人|language=ja}}</ref>
